Authors: Hongzhe Zhao; Pengcheng Li; Yanqing Wang; Picheng Chen; Yu Ding; Yuetao Liu; Fengchen Qiao; Yumin Wu; Li Ding; Chuanhui Gao
Title: Sustainable closed-loop recycling of vinylogous urethan-based covalent adaptable networks: Impact of branching nodes on mechanical strength and recyclability
Keywords: CAN; vinylogous urethane; recycling; reprocessing; dynamic covalent network
Key Findings: Branching-node design improves mechanical properties and dynamic bond exchange; closed-loop chemical recycling was demonstrated
Important Data: Thermal and solvent recycling retained >85% performance after three cycles; acidolysis recovered approximately 80–85% reusable monomers
Notes: Useful for CAN reprocessing/recycling discussion and comparison with GFLA-3

Authors: Ning Zheng; Yang Xu; Qian Zhao; Tao Xie
Title: Dynamic Covalent Polymer Networks: A Molecular Platform for Designing Functions beyond Chemical Recycling and Self-Healing
Keywords: dynamic covalent network; chemical recycling; self-healing; shape-shifting
Key Findings: Dynamic bond exchange enables network reconfiguration and supports chemical recycling, self-healing, shape-shifting and other functions
Notes: Useful for GFLA-3 discussion of dynamic covalent networks and reconfiguration

Authors: Matthew K. McBride; Brady T. Worrell; Tobin Brown; Lewis M. Cox; Nancy Sowan; Chen Wang; Maciej Podgorski; Alina M. Martinez; Christopher N. Bowman
Title: Enabling Applications of Covalent Adaptable Networks
Journal: Annual Review of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
Keywords: CAN; vitrimer; recyclable polymer; shape-memory polymer; thermoset
Key Findings: CANs combine thermoset-like crosslinking with dynamic exchange, enabling reprocessing and applications including shape-memory polymers
Notes: Useful for introducing the concept and applications of CANs

Authors: Siyang Wang; Lei Li; Marek W. Urban
Title: Combined Reprocessability and Self-Healing in Fluorinated Acrylic-Based Covalent Adaptable Networks (CANs)
Key Findings: The CANs show reprocessability and self-healing through dynamic vinylogous urethane chemistry
Important Data: Maximum stress at break about 16 MPa; reprocessable by compression molding at 120 °C
Notes: Useful for comparing reprocessing and self-healing of GFLA-3

Authors: Maxime Houbben; Clara Pereira Sanchez; Philippe Vanderbemden; Ludovic Noels; Christine Jerome
Title: MWCNTs filled PCL covalent adaptable networks: Towards reprocessable, self-healing and fast electrically-triggered shape-memory composites
Keywords: CAN; PCL; shape-memory; self-healing; recycling; electrical actuation
Key Findings: PCL-CAN composites combine shape memory, network reconfiguration, self-healing and recyclability; MWCNTs enable electrical actuation
Notes: Very relevant to shape-memory and reprocessable CAN comparison

Authors: Zepeng Lei; Hongxuan Chen; Shaofeng Huang; Lacey J. Wayment; Qiucheng Xu; Wei Zhang
Title: New Advances in Covalent Network Polymers via Dynamic Covalent Chemistry
Keywords: dynamic covalent chemistry; covalent network; reprocessing; recyclability; crystallinity
